Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for West Indies' reply. The umpires are out and are followed by the England players who are spreading across the field. Brandon King and Evin Lewis are the openers for West Indies! Jofra Archer has the new ball in hand and is raring to go! Away we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

With the momentum now firmly on their side, England head into the defence of a very respectable 263, quite a turnaround on a ground notorious for tough defences! They’ll still need sharp, disciplined bowling from the outset to keep West Indies under pressure and make early inroads. For the hosts, it’s all about starting strong. A solid foundation from the top order will be crucial to chasing this total down, allowing them to take control and avoid any mid-innings drama. We’re all set for a gripping second innings!

Phil Salt is in for a chat. He says that as a team, they are happy where they are at in the game. Shares that he would have loved to get a three-figure score. Mentions that it was hard work early on against the new ball. Feels that this is a good batting effort considering the position they were in at 24/4. Reckons that they can defend this score if they get a few early wickets.

Undeterred, Phil Salt continued to bat with caution and notched up a well-deserved half-century. Brandon King then produced a sensational catch to dismiss Salt, breaking a crucial partnership at a pivotal moment. Dan Mousley, then shifted gears to inject much-needed momentum into the innings. Teaming up with Jamie Overton, Mousley took full advantage of West Indies’ depleted death bowling, with Romario Shepherd sidelined due to a left-leg injury. Mousley’s maiden half-century was crucial, helping propel England past the 200-run mark but it was Jofra Archer's late surge that pushed them to a total they will fancy defending.

The defining blow came with the prized wicket of England’s captain, Liam Livingstone, fresh off a century in the previous game. Romario Shepherd’s delivery found its mark, sending Livingstone back to the pavilion and leaving England in dire straits at 24/4 just around the 10-over mark. Struggling to find any momentum, England seemed on the brink, until Sam Curran stepped in with resolve. Curran’s steady presence alongside Phil Salt offered a glimmer of hope, as the pair set about stabilizing the innings. With a few confident strokes to break the tension, Curran and Salt managed to craft a crucial 70-run partnership that gave England a foothold in the game. However, their hard work was disrupted when Roston Chase claimed Curran’s wicket, setting England back once more and forcing them to start from scratch.

After winning the toss and, unsurprisingly, choosing to bowl first, Shai Hope and West Indies couldn’t have scripted a better start. Matthew Forde led the charge with early aggression, striking in the third over to dismiss Will Jacks and ignite the pressure on England. The pacers maintained impeccable lines and lengths, reeling in two more quick wickets, one for Alzarri Joseph and another for Romario Shepherd, putting England firmly on the back foot.

What an unexpected twist to the innings! Just when it seemed England’s scoring had stalled, Jofra Archer delivered a breathtaking cameo, smashing 38 off just 17 balls to propel England to a competitive 263/8. His late blitz injected a surge of momentum, catching West Indies off guard and giving England’s bowlers a stronger total to defend than anyone anticipated.

Another brace to end the innings! Slower and around off, on a short of a length, Archer stays back and flat-bats it down the ground. Adil wants to come back for the second run but he gets sent back initially by Archer before being called through for the run. The throw from the deep is wayward and it is well wide of the bowler, allowing the batters to complete the second run comfortably. 25 runs off the over. England finish with 263/8.

We are moments away from the first ball in this series decider, but before that, the match officials, the two sets of players, and their mascots will line up for the national anthems. First up will be the national anthem of Barbados, followed by England’s and then the anthem of the West Indies.

Jacob Bethell is also down for a chat. He says he is very proud of the way he played in the previous game and hopes to continue. Adds that he is very excited to be a part of this series decider. Talks about Liam Livingstone and says there wasn't too much talk and Liam just came out and put the pressure back on the bowlers straightaway. Concludes that Sam Curran played his role in the previous game and hopes for both of them to help Livingstone this time around.

PITCH REPORT - Nikhil Uttamchandani is near the deck. He starts by saying that there is a 3-metre difference between the square boundaries with 64 metres to one side and 61 to the other. Adds that it is 73 metres down the ground. Feels that wind will be a factor that batters will have to take into account while clearing the boundaries. Informs that out of the 11 ODIs played here since 2020, 9 of them have been won by the chasing side. Carlos Brathwaite joins him and says that batters should look to hit straight. From a bowler's perspective, he feels that they should force the batters to hit towards the longer of the two square boundaries and use the wind to their advantage.

Shimron Hetmyer is down for a quick chat. He says he has stopped overthinking about his game and has started to enjoy it, which is showing in the way he is playing. He talks about one outing here five years ago, where he scored a century against England. Adds he was really young in the squad, which now brings a lot of fond memories, and it's very special to play against England at Barbados.

Adds that this is a ground that heavily favours the chasing side and therefore, they would have loved to chase. Mentions that they will see what the pitch has to offer and hopes that the game goes well for them. Feels that they will need to assess the conditions quickly and take it from there. Informs that they have made two changes - Reece Topley and Jamie Overton are in for Saqib Mahmood and John Turner. Shares that they want to play an attacking brand of cricket and put the opposition under pressure.

Shai Hope, the skipper of West Indies says they aren't quite sure of how the pitch will play like and want to chase. Adds that they will have to assess the conditions quickly and play really well. With both teams eager to clinch the series, this final match promises intense competition. England will seek to capitalize on their recent momentum, while the West Indies will be looking to leverage their home advantage and reclaim dominance. Expect an action-packed series decider. Stick around for the toss and team news.

On the West Indies side, Shai Hope and Evin Lewis have been pivotal in the hosts' batting lineup. Hope, who has amassed 123 runs in two games, including a memorable century in the second ODI, was instrumental in giving the team a competitive total last time around. Keacy Carty and Sherfane Rutherford have also contributed valuable middle-order runs, giving West Indies stability.
